messages:
Sophia: FYI saw a perf/cost blip when a customer sent mixed-dimension batches to /v1/embeddings. Console only showed a latency spike, no signal about why we split. Proposal: add a lightweight client-provided shape hint header to aid routing and surface predicted splits in Console. Thoughts?

Alex: I'm +1 for visibility. Router already runs a preflight for large payloads; exposing its estimate should be low-risk. Q: do we record estimates for every request? could be noisy. Maybe only when mixed dims detected or payload > X bytes.

Kai: runtime note: computing an exact split plan requires scanning payload which is costly at high QPS. A header like `X-Embed-Shape: 12x768,4x1024` lets us shortcut. If header absent we sample first N items to approximate. We can also accept a compressed form like `768:12;1024:4`.

Jordan: UX: add a small Console CTA: "Enable shape hints" with one-click SDK snippets that inject the header when batching client-side. Also we should show a per-route banner when mixed-dim traffic exceeds 1% of requests.

Maria: Dashboard: show predicted vs actual split_count time series and a heatmap by client showing mixed-dim frequency. Add an alert when actual/predicted > 1.5 over a 5m window. Product also wants a helper: "Reduce splits" with suggestions (pad to uniform dim or client-side homogeneous batching) and estimated cost/latency tradeoffs.

Alex: Billing/console semantics: if we split a request internally, charge aggregated billed tokens. Console should show total billed tokens and an optional breakdown line for internal split overhead so teams can correlate cost spikes to splitting.

Sophia: Important: malformed hint header must be non-fatal. If parse fails, fallback to sampling and emit telemetry `embed.shape_hint_malformed`. Dont reject requests.

Kai: Prefetch optimization: if hint shows groups by dim, runtime can prefetch per-dim KV/cache to avoid repeated work. But prefetch needs quota/backpressure controls. Propose per-customer flag `embed.prefetch_enabled` and metric `embed.prefetch_tokens_inflight`.

Jordan: Rollout plan: canary shape-hint parsing on 10% of traffic with metric `embed.shape_hint_used`. Console rollout panel should include tiny AB charts for latency delta, cost delta, and split_accuracy (predicted==actual).

Maria: SDKs default: when user calls Embeddings.batch(inputs), SDK should compute dims and auto-add header for batched homogeneous or mixed batches (opt-in in config). Add docs page "Shape hints and routing" with examples.

Sophia: Example header snippet:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
X-Embed-Shape: 9x512,6x768
Content-Type: application/json
{ "inputs": [ ... ] }
```

Alex: Telemetry keys to add: `embed.predicted_splits`, `embed.actual_splits`, `embed.split_accuracy`, `embed.estimated_billed_tokens`, `embed.actual_billed_tokens`, `embed.shape_hint_missing` (bool), `embed.shape_hint_malformed` (bool). Capture per-route and per-customer.

Kai: Ops caveat: prediction heuristics will have edgecases (padding strategies, tokenization differences, quantization variants). Start conservative: require split_accuracy >= 0.7 in canary before enabling broader rollouts.

Jordan: Console UX idea: clicking a route shows an overlay timeline that compares predicted vs actual splits; hovering a point shows quick reasoning: e.g., "mixed dims 512/768 -> 3 splits, padded vs not padded". Good for debugging large customers.

Maria: Product ask: surface automated suggestions in Console: "Pad to 768 (estimated cost +1.8%) or split client-side into homogenous batches (estimated latency -12ms)". This helps customers choose a strategy.

Sophia: Action items: 1) Kai: implement header parsing + sampling fallback (canary 10%) 2) Alex: add telemetry keys + backend endpoints for predicted vs actual 3) Jordan: design small Console visuals and rollout panel 4) Maria: docs + SDK templates 5) Ops: add backpressure metrics and per-customer prefetch toggle. I'll open tickets and link here. Thanks :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploybot: schedule canary deploy for embed-shape-hint parser to staging at 2026-03-22T18:30:00Z

Alex: note on perf: if parsing/estimation adds >1ms p50 we should move it off the critical path or only enable for customers above volume threshold. Default should be off for low-volume customers to avoid regressions.
